summary: This diff wires gitleaks/trivy/checkov into a real, cron-scheduled security scanner pipeline (ai-os-scripts/audit_pipeline_security.py) that writes normalized findings into new audit_findings/audit_runs sqlite tables, plus commits previously live-only Phase 0/1 auditor-engine planning artifacts and reconciles drift in MASTER_INDEX.yaml. The script is architecturally sound: all subprocess calls use list-form args (no shell injection), all DB writes are parameterized (no SQL injection), it correctly redacts gitleaks' raw Secret/Match fields before persisting raw_json and never includes secret plaintext in finding text, and it reuses the existing flock write-lock convention shared with other writers of the same DB (verified against file_inventory.py). The finding-record and event JSON schemas are valid JSON; the phase-plan and MASTER_INDEX YAML parse cleanly. The large MASTER_INDEX.yaml diff (1916+/1412-) looked alarming at first glance but is confirmed legitimate: mostly a block-scalar rewrap plus real drift-reconciliation content (restoring/aligning entries from concurrent already-approved tasks), not data loss or scope creep -- no registry entries were dropped and no secrets are exposed in it. The new crontab entry and its 'blanket approval' citation in OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_2026-07-23.yaml are legitimate: the task's own dispatched prompt.txt (line 13) explicitly pre-authorizes this exact citation pattern, so this is not a self-invented approval. No .github/workflows/** changes are present. Given the diff touches a 'security' path and a crontab modification, tier2 (human sign-off before merge) is the correct classification, and this record is only a recommendation that a human proceed with merge -- not a merge action itself.
issues: Correctness/completeness gap in audit_pipeline_security.py's upsert_findings(): a finding that stops being detected on a later scan (i.e. the underlying issue was fixed) is never transitioned to 'resolved' -- there is no reconciliation step that closes prior 'open' rows absent from the current run's record set. Over repeated nightly runs, audit_findings.status='open' will accumulate stale/no-longer-true findings, undermining the pipeline's value as a current audit signal. Worth a fast follow-up task to add a per-repo/per-tool 'mark rows not seen this run as resolved' step.

Commit message for 8694342 doesn't mention that it also substantively reworded the testing_engine_irvf entry and added a new note_on_repo_vs_live_drift field to the unrelated terminology_standardization entry in MASTER_INDEX.yaml -- both are legitimate drift-reconciliation (not scope creep), but the commit message under-describes scope for future auditability.

Human sign-off should independently confirm the live crontab (`crontab -l` on the Hetzner server) actually matches the new CRONTAB_APPROVED_SNAPSHOT.txt entry for audit-pipeline-security, since crontab changes are a standing exception under AI_ENGINEERING_POLICY.yaml even when pre-authorized by the dispatched task prompt.
